messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert P-47F2 triggered for node failure - host=gpu-rack-13-host-7, symptom=kubelet NotReady, pods evicted. Severity: page

pagerduty: Paging morgan (primary oncall) for P-47F2. Reason: host unreachable, syslogs show kernel OOPS around network driver.

morgan: acked. looking now. tell me if any customer-facing routes are degraded.

ryan: seeing a handful of 5xx from /v1/generate across region-us-west1. 8% error rate on our routing dashboard, spikes started ~2m ago.

morgan: ok prioritizing node. grabbing kube node status.

morgan: `kubectl get nodes gpu-rack-13-host-7 -o wide` -> STATUS: NotReady, REASON: KubeletNotReady

morgan: `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` shows repeated: 
```
Oct 12 03:12:09 gpu-rack-13-host-7 kernel: NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
Oct 12 03:12:11 gpu-rack-13-host-7 kernel: kernel: nvidia: GPU HANG detected
Oct 12 03:12:14 kubelet[1234]: node status report: kubelet stopped responding to healthz
```

sam: also seeing failed mounts for /dev/nvme0n1s1 in dmesg on that host. could be disk + driver flakiness.

morgan: good catch. risk of data corruption if we try reboot now. plan: cordon + drain remaining pods off host, spin short-lived replacement node from spare pool, notify routing to stop sending new requests to that rack.

ryan: thumbs up. I'll open a temporary routing rule to shift traffic off rack-13, reduce impact.

morgan: `kubectl cordon gpu-rack-13-host-7` -> node cordoned.
morgan: starting `kubectl drain gpu-rack-13-host-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> 12 pods evicted. Some model-serving pods failed to reschedule immediately due to resource constraints.

devon: I'm standing up a replacement host from the Dedicated spare pool (dedicated-spare-1). will attach same instance profile and label it for GPU workloads. ETA ~3m.

pagerduty: Escalation timer: 10m until manager-level alert if unresolved.

morgan: adding temporary autoscale: increase replica counts for critical model-serving deployments to absorb capacity loss. `kubectl scale deploy/redwood-gpt --replicas=24`

sam: after scale, errors dropped to ~1.2% but latency increased ~120ms on p50 for short window. routing change holding. no currently blocked customers flagged in SCC.

morgan: good. continuing with host investigation. ssh to BMC shows host reachable at IPMI, but host OS not responding to systemctl. my hunch: GPU driver kernel oops + NVMe errors.

morgan: starting a graceful soft-reboot via IPMI (sol command) to avoid forcing NVMe state. notifying infra runbook owners.

incident-bot: action recorded - soft-reboot initiated by morgan at 1934568001.

morgan: reboot came up but kubelet still not becoming ready; kubelet logs after reboot show repeated nvme I/O failures and device removal. suspect underlying NVMe failure.

devon: replacement host is ready and labeled. shifting pods. writing a quick drain-and-migrate playbook to the thread: 
```
- cordon old
- drain old
- label new host gpu=true
- taint removal
- scale down old deployments (if stuck)
```

morgan: migration completed. all critical model-serving pods on replacement host. health checks green, error rate back to baseline. rollback autoscale to normal.

pagerduty: Incident P-47F2 marked as "mitigated" by morgan at 1934568420.

morgan: handing off to devon for follow-up (hardware replacement ticket, post-incident infra action). devon, can you take on remediation and BLAM items?

devon: taking handoff. I'll open ticket to RMA NVMe, schedule host replacement, and draft a postmortem with timeline + mitigation suggestions (improve prewarming for spare pool, add NVMe SMART alerts in monitoring).

sam: adding note: consider disabling aggressive GC on models during node moves to reduce transient latency.

morgan: quick customer impact summary for postmortem: brief elevated 5xx (~8% for ~4 minutes), increased latency p50 +120ms during autoscale; no sustained data loss. Affected: subset of hosted customers in us-west1 routed to rack-13.

devon: will include that in the postmortem. handoff complete. closing thread after write-up. :white_check_mark:
